insights.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue rose to ₹256 Cr with a 25.2% EBITDA margin (28.3% before a ₹7.8 Cr Ind AS 29 charge) and PAT of ₹47 Cr; the order book jumped to ₹1,945 Cr (1.9x last year's revenue), led by energy storage at Endoks. Management held FY27 guidance at ~20% growth and an EBITDA margin of 20% or high teens, warned of a dip in standalone margins in Q3 as the new Sangli plant's costs arrive before revenue (expected from Q3, meaningful in Q4), and reiterated ~50% growth for FY28. It is buying Winwin (ex-WS) Insulators at an EV of ~₹315 Cr and plans to raise under ₹500 Cr.

what_changed.text: ~20% revenue growth in FY27; may revisit at Q3
EBITDA margin guidance: 20% or high teens
Sangli: trial production in August; revenue from Q3, meaningful only in Q4
Acquiring Winwin Speciality Insulators (EV ~₹315 Cr), consolidation from Q4
Mehru margin guidance raised to ~18% from above 15%
Fund-raise of under ₹500 Cr, road shows from 20 August

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: Getting orders is not a worry at this moment for us.

analyst_questions.answer: Aluminium bought now reaches coil production ~6 months later; Sangli fixed costs arrive before volumes. Coil business 'stable guidance' ~20%, orders booked above 25%.
Insulators are the industry bottleneck; WS is approved in 55+ countries; paid ~₹50-60 Cr for the business plus 40 acres of land.
Awaiting building completion and other statutory approvals; then ~60 customer audits over ~6 months.
Their Indian plants are mostly idle; local-content rules still apply.

red_flags.text: Sangli plant start has slipped from June to August, with revenue only from Q3.
Another equity raise (under ₹500 Cr) within 18 months of the IPO, for acquisitions and a US entry.
Winwin plant has a troubled history (cyclone write-off, gas-crisis losses) and needs a turnaround.
Cash balances fell as expansion is funded internally.

watch_next: Q2 revenue growth vs ~20% and EBITDA margin vs 20%
Sangli commercial production and customer audits
Winwin acquisition closing and size of the fund-raise
PCS factory start at Endoks in Q3
